title: icbinr-gpwa-email
label: Jordan Stone

won.source: No record of how or when this reign began survives; named the GPWA's own E-Mail Champion by the site index's own later, undated snapshot -- the fed's own served Site Index page (promotions/icbinr/archive/index.html)

how: Not documented in the held record.
note: Stone's only card win in the held record (over Commander Cody at Slamfest, 17 May 1998) is never billed as a title match in the card's own text -- recorded separately, never assumed to be the same event.

title: icbinr-gpwa-heavyweight
label: The Angry Chef

won.source: Bracketed between two dated facts, neither one the win itself: the fed's own 19 March 1998 On The Road advanced Chef to the tournament final over Poe (Card Summaries), and the Topeka Tabloid's own 5 October 1998 recap already bills him "the reigning Great Plains Heavyweight Champion" retaining, not winning, the belt (the fed's own served Regional News page, 5/28/1999 (promotions/icbinr/archive/regional-news-1999-05-28.html)). The tournament final itself (Chef vs. Emerald) is never shown.

how: Won the GPWA Heavyweight Championship Tournament; the final round is not documented.
note: Defended twice in one night at the Topeka Civic Center, 5 October 1998, against Commander Cody and #1 contender Jack Emerald (icbinr-topeka-civic-center-1998-10-05); also defended against Dane Thompson at an untranscribed "GPWA Slim Pickens" (rib injury), per the 1998-09-28 news item -- that show is not itself structured, no date surviving beyond "before 1998-09-28." By the site index's own later, undated snapshot the belt had changed hands to "Sideshow" Tad Detmer; no document shows how.

title: icbinr-gpwa-heavyweight
label: Hawk Hunter

won.source: "GPWA House Show Results" (2 May 1999): "Sideshow" Tad Detmer hands over the Great Plains Heavyweight Championship to Hawk Hunter in an on-air agreement.

how: Awarded on air by the outgoing champion's own agreement, not by pinfall.
note: Still champion at the close of this reading's own 1999 pull, which ends 18 May 1999, ten days before the wing's own already-recorded 28 May 1999 closing window.

title: icbinr-gpwa-tag
label: Thunder & Lightning

won.source: The fed's own served Card Summaries page: "Small Package (February 28, 1998)... 4-way match for the GPWA Tag Team Championship... Thunder pins Belliel with the Rainmaker... Thunder & Lightning crowned GPWA Tag Team Champions."

how: Won a four-way match at "Small Package," pinning Belliel of the Princes of Darkness.
note: Successfully defended against Hiroki Date & Ron Baxter on 24 May 1998 ("Thunder pins Date with a Powerslam"), the held record's latest dated card result. By the time of the site index's own later, undated snapshot the belt had changed hands to The Man & The Myth -- no document in the held record shows how or when.

title: icbinr-us-heavyweight
label: Reginald Parkhurst III

won.source: "McManus's loss to Reginald Parkhurst III at ICBINR End Of The Beginning for the United States Heavyweight Title" (1999-02-22 news item); "current ICBINR U.S. Heavyweight Champion, Reginald Parkhurst III" (1999-03-29 news item); "End of the Beginning" dated by the 1999-01-05 item's own "recent New Years Eve event." -- the fed's own served Regional News page, 5/28/1999 (promotions/icbinr/archive/regional-news-1999-05-28.html)

how: Defeated Nate McManus at End of the Beginning for the vacant title, after winning a 4-Corners qualifier (against Jack Emerald, Kai A. Lewis and "Sideshow" Tad Detmer) whose own date, venue and finish are not documented in the held record.
note: The inaugural reign -- the title had never had a champion before this win. Still champion by the held record's latest dated mention (29 March 1999) and the site index's own later, undated snapshot alike.
